original_question: Can the McKay correspondence be generalized to more general groups and group schemes, including positive-dimensional algebraic groups, abelian varieties, non-reduced finite group schemes, and profinite groups?
target_in_paper: Section 10, Problem 10.2: the open problem asking for a generalization of the paper’s McKay correspondence to more general groups/group schemes, explicitly including positive-dimensional algebraic groups, abelian varieties, non-reduced finite group schemes, and pro-finite groups. The introduction also says that Section 10 is where the paper discusses generalizations of the McKay correspondence and motivic integration. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it identifies the correct target problem, keeps the same four example classes of groups/group schemes, and does not drift into a neighboring topic. In substance, it matches Problem 10.2 almost verbatim. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
missing_details: The paper means the wild/stringy-motivic McKay correspondence reviewed earlier in Section 2.3, not a different variant such as the derived McKay correspondence of Section 12 or the global-fields problem of Section 13. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

By the paper’s stated convention, the base field is assumed algebraically closed unless otherwise specified; your draft leaves that ambient assumption implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
Problem 10.2 is posed as an open problem, not as a theorem, proposition, or formal conjecture with a fixed hypothesis list. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The examples in Problem 10.2 are illustrative rather than exhaustive: the wording is about more general groups/group schemes ‘such as’ the listed classes, so the scope is broader than exactly four examples but should still stay within this specific generalization problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

Nearby context shows that this problem is tied to constructing moduli spaces for more general group schemes (Problem 8.3), and is closely related—but not stated to be equivalent—to generalizing motivic integration to Artin stacks (Problem 10.3). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The paper does not impose extra degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or ‘for sufficiently large’ conditions here; adding such hypotheses would make the question less faithful to Problem 10.2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
refined_question: In the paper’s stringy-motivic sense of the wild McKay correspondence, and over the paper’s default algebraically closed base field, can one generalize the McKay correspondence to more general groups or group schemes, specifically including positive-dimensional algebraic groups, abelian varieties, non-reduced finite group schemes, and pro-finite groups? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
justification: This draft clearly targets Section 10 rather than any statement in the introduction. The paper first defines the relevant McKay correspondence in Section 2.3 as the wild/stringy-motivic correspondence, then announces in the introduction that Section 10 concerns generalizations of the McKay correspondence and motivic integration, and finally states Problem 10.2 in essentially the same terms as your draft. The nearest precision supplied by nearby context is not a reformulation but supporting infrastructure: Problem 8.3 points to moduli spaces for more general group schemes, while Problem 10.3 is said to be closely related because Artin-stack motivic integration is expected to matter here. So the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is to keep Problem 10.2 narrow, anchor ‘McKay correspondence’ to the Section 2.3 wild/stringy-motivic framework, and avoid broadening the question into the separate mixed-characteristic, derived, or global-fields problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
